settings.title: Frequently Asked Questions
settings.question_1: What's the difference between this and a regular blood pressure supplement?
settings.answer_1: Blood pressure supplements target vasodilation, relaxing vessel walls to lower pressure. That's one mechanism. Hemo Flow targets viscosity, the mechanical thickness of blood itself. Fibrin accumulation, RBC stiffness, and plasma resistance are the upstream drivers most supplements never address. Different layer, different outcome.
settings.answer_2: Most men notice energy, circulation warmth, and gym changes in weeks 4–7. Blood pressure shifts register by week 8. Don't quit at week 3. The mechanism, fibrin clearance and RBC deformability improvement — takes time to build. Give it the full cycle.
settings.question_3: Why does the label show FU and SPU units instead of milligrams?
settings.answer_3: FU (fibrinolytic units) measures nattokinase enzymatic activity — the actual potency, not the weight. SPU measures serrapeptase. Most products show milligrams, which tells you nothing about how active the ingredient is. We use the units the clinical research uses. Cross-reference it yourself.
settings.question_4: Is it safe to stack with other supplements?
settings.answer_4: Yes for most protocols — fish oil, magnesium, zinc, creatine, standard vitamins, TRT. One flag: if you're on prescription anticoagulants (warfarin, Eliquis, Plavix), check with your doctor first. Nattokinase has mild fibrinolytic activity that can compound prescription blood thinners. For everything else — it stacks cleanly.
